parsed.main_gap: The key constructive step of the refinement lemma's upper bound (Xiang's overlay cuts realizing D=Γ within q-1 cuts) is asserted as "standard; details omitted", including the tight cut count.

errors.description: The heart of Xiang's explicit strategy — overlaying the A-row and B-row, taking the common refinement, and checking that the total number of new cuts (including the cut at the point corresponding to s_B, which makes the bound exactly q-1 and hence tight) is at most q-1 — is not carried out. The reconstruction is routine but the count is delicate and unverified.
errors.quote: and use at most \(q-1\) cuts in total (standard; details omitted).

errors.description: The "grid example" is claimed to agree with the theorem, but for Liu's split (7,14,35)/56 one has Γ = 7/56 = 1/8, so the game value of that split is 9/16, not 4/7; Xiang's marks (8,38) are suboptimal. The agreement is coincidental. (Flagged as evidence, not proof, so harmless.)
errors.quote:
Sorting gives Liu
\((18+13+1)/56=32/56=4/7\), in agreement with the theorem.

errors.description: Sections 5–6 are largely extraneous (falsification log, references to scripts) and do not contribute to the argument; the assertion that a Liu mark coinciding with an overlay boundary "only reduce[s] the cut count" is stated without checking it cannot also destroy the pairing structure (it does not, but this is unargued).
errors.quote:
An overlay boundary already equal to a Liu mark requires no new mark, so
coincidences only reduce the cut count.

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) checks out; greedy drafting lemma, the tree/bipartition lower bound D ≥ Γ, and the subset-sum pigeonhole are all correct and rigorously done. Only the constructive half of the refinement lemma is sketched.
